one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, statistically rigorous test of how much of the accuracy gain from a retrieved procedural-memory bank (ExpeL-style, ReasoningBank-style) survives once a GEPA-optimized instruction is trained on the identical episodes, quantified as a substitution ratio S (superiority-at-baseline plus TOST-equivalence-at-optimized conjunction), with matched-token compiled-bank and whole-bank-dump control arms and a synthetic non-compilable positive control that must show low substitution to certify the instrument works.
closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal's own collision check surfaces and concedes is 'the three-way comparison v2 said did not exist': it already runs a memory retriever (Memento, ReasoningBank) and GEPA on a shared 528/267 training/test trajectory split across four domains and three backbones, and reports that no automatic method dominates every cell. The proposal's genuinely new material relative to it -- the combined optimizer+memory cells (I2xM1, I2xM0), the token-matched compiled and whole-bank arms, the coverage-matched bank, the substitution-ratio statistic with paired equivalence testing, and the B-dup positive control -- is real methodological machinery, but it is an instrumentation upgrade on an already-published table rather than a newly discovered phenomenon.
strongest_objection: The research-track brief this was written for requires 'Small open-weight models (7B-32B class)... The interesting result must not depend on frontier-scale models,' yet the primary, 'load-bearing' agent A1 is gpt-oss-120b, chosen explicitly because it is the one agent (of two tested in the cited pilot study) where the ExpeL bank showed a nonzero memory effect (+7.7pt); the in-scope Qwen3.5-27B model showed the same bank's effect as TOST-equivalent to zero and is demoted to a secondary 'degenerate regime' arm on a reduced grid (A2, condition 11 in the falsifiable predictions). This means that within the track's own declared model-scale scope, the phenomenon the whole study exists to explain -- memory helping, and whether that help survives prompt optimization -- is never actually observed; the central substitution claim is only testable by stepping outside the stated resource/scope envelope. Given that the related literature the proposal itself cites (EvoAgentBench's '+7 on Qwen backbones' for ReasoningBank) suggests an in-scope memory-positive setup exists, choosing to escalate to a 120B model instead reads as reaching for the agent scale that produces the desired effect rather than testing the claim where the track asked it to be tested.
what_would_fix_it: Swap or supplement A1 with an in-scope 7B-32B agent that shows a genuine memory effect with a real memory method -- e.g., ReasoningBank on a Qwen-class backbone, which EvoAgentBench's own results (cited in this proposal's Related Work) already report as positive -- so the substitution question is answered inside the track's actual resource constraints rather than requiring escalation to a 120B MoE model. Separately, cut the combinatorial scope: 14 primary cells x up to 4 optimizer seeds x 2 agents x 2 environments x a LoRA-SFT arm x human-validated moderator labeling is closer to two or three papers' worth of experiments than the 'days, not weeks' the brief specifies, and trimming it (the proposal's own 'ordered contingency cuts' list is a good starting point for what to drop preemptively) would materially reduce execution risk.
missing_baseline: ReasoningBank (rather than ExpeL) evaluated on an in-scope Qwen-class (7B-32B) backbone, which the proposal's own cited source (EvoAgentBench) reports produces a real, non-null memory effect (~+7pt); the plan instead builds another ExpeL bank and escalates to an out-of-scope 120B agent to find a nonzero effect to substitute away, without ever showing that its central phenomenon exists on a model the track's brief actually licenses.
preprint_collision: This is a genuinely strong collision check, better than most: a dated scan (2026-09-03, with a prior 2026-08-21 pass noted), 15 HF Papers queries, by-id abstract verification for 54 arXiv IDs, cross-channel web-search corroboration where arXiv itself was unreachable, a committed log file, and -- most tellingly -- an honest retraction: on finding EvoAgentBench, the proposal withdraws its own prior claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other,' and separately reinstates five citations a previous version had wrongly dropped for being 'unverifiable.' That said, the check itself flags unresolved residual risk (NeurIPS 2026 camera-readies surfacing in October, a possible buried 'GEPA + memory' ablation in some systems paper's appendix) and commits only to re-running the scan before freeze and submission -- so the novelty finding is provisional, and the proposal's remaining novelty claim rests on a fairly narrow set of measurement additions (paired substitution ratio, compiled/whole-bank arms, positive control) layered on top of EvoAgentBench's already-published three-way table.
